title: Every invariant element of a quotient lifts to a monic invariant polynomial mapping to its nth power

standard_prerequisites.name: Action of a finite group on a ring map and the invariant subrings A^G and B^G
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes sense of the requirement that P lie in A^G[T] and that its image lie in B^G[T].

standard_prerequisites.name: Multiplicativity of a ring map on products and the fact that an invariant element is fixed by every group element
standard_prerequisites.use: Is what lets the image of prod (T - sigma(a)) be identified with prod (T - b) = (T - b)^n.

core_obligations: Choose a lift a in A of the given element b of B^G, using that A -> B is surjective (proof line 32548).
Set P = prod_{sigma in G} (T - sigma(a)) and observe that P is monic of degree n = |G| (proof line 32549).

Verify that P is invariant under the action of G on A[T], so that P lies in A^G[T], by permuting the factors of the product (construction at proof line 32549, statement conclusion at lines 32543-32544).
Verify that the image of P in B^G[T] is (T - b)^n, since each sigma(a) maps to b and b is fixed by G (statement conclusion at lines 32543-32544).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a surjection of rings varphi : A -> B, a finite group G of order n acting on that map, and an element b of the invariant subring B^G, and asserts the existence of a monic polynomial P in A^G[T] which maps to (T - b)^n in B^G[T] (source lines 32539-32545). The construction is explicit: choose a lift a of b in A and set P = prod_{sigma in G} (T - sigma(a)) (proof lines 32547-32549). What has to be checked is that this P really lies in the invariant subring A^G[T], that it is monic of degree n, and that its image in B^G[T] is (T - b)^n, which uses that b is fixed by G so that every sigma acts on b trivially. Those verifications are not written out by the author.
